position_a: Use delay or short filtered ambience to preserve intelligibility and avoid a washed lead.
position_b: Reverb is a normal and valuable vocal tool when decay, predelay, filtering, and level fit the song.
tutor_behavior: Do not forbid either tool. Offer a level-matched A/B with separate wet auxes.
what_decides: Arrangement density, genre, desired depth, phrase spacing, and whether the effect masks consonants.

position_a: Multiple real takes can create density and width.
position_b: A strong single lead often preserves clarity, intimacy, and emotional focus better.
tutor_behavior: Compare one, two, and three takes at matched total loudness; never call triple tracking universally professional.
what_decides: Performance consistency, genre, desired scale, lyric intelligibility, and arrangement.

position_a: Compression provides short-term control and density.
position_b: Manual/recorded rides place phrases and syllables more musically.
tutor_behavior: Use clip gain, moderate compression, and automation as complementary rather than exclusive.
what_decides: Time scale of the problem. Extreme local outliers, short-term envelope, and section-level placement need different tools.

position_a: High-pass filtering can remove rumble, plosives, and unnecessary low energy.
position_b: Aggressive filtering can remove chest, warmth, and low-register identity.
tutor_behavior: Raise cutoff while listening in context, then back off; do not provide one universal frequency.
what_decides: Singer, mic distance, lowest notes, arrangement, and whether low energy is actually problematic.

position_a: A de-esser gives consistent dynamic frequency control.
position_b: Manual clip gain/automation can be more transparent for isolated or highly variable consonants.
tutor_behavior: Calibrate DeEsser 2 conservatively and use local edits for outliers.
what_decides: How frequent and consistent the sibilance is, and whether automated reduction causes lisping/darkness.

position_a: One well-set compressor is simpler and easier to diagnose.
position_b: Two modest stages with distinct jobs can sound smoother than one stage doing heavy work.
tutor_behavior: Require each stage to have a named job and level-match the alternatives.
what_decides: Peak behavior, leveling need, desired color, and total accumulated gain reduction.

position_a: Stronger correction can meet a polished genre expectation.
position_b: Selective correction preserves vibrato, drift, and identity.
topic: Perfect pitch correction versus preserving natural pitch motion
tutor_behavior: Start selective; compare corrected and original phrases, not only blobs.
what_decides: Genre, performance, desired aesthetic, artifact audibility, and emotional role.

position_a: Sends provide independent wet processing, sharing, filtering, and automation.
position_b: Insert effects are valid for deliberate serial transformations or simple self-contained chains.
topic: Using reverb/delay as insert versus send
tutor_behavior: Default to wet aux for conventional mix effects but explain exceptions.
what_decides: Need for independent dry level, shared space, automation, and creative topology.

position_a: Source changes can solve performance, plosive, room, and mic-position problems cleanly.
position_b: Editing/restoration is appropriate when the performance is irreplaceable or re-recording is impossible.
tutor_behavior: Run a short re-record test before a large repair workflow when feasible.
what_decides: Artistic value of take, artifact severity, time, repeatability, and repair transparency.

position_a: Solo helps locate noise, resonances, and edit artifacts.
position_b: Full-mix context decides balance, masking, and whether a tonal change is useful.
topic: EQ in solo versus in the mix
tutor_behavior: Move between views deliberately; never finalize context-dependent EQ in solo alone.
what_decides: Diagnostic stage. Use solo to inspect, context to decide.

position_a: Smart preserves relative ordering and expressive internal relationships.
position_b: Classic provides direct grid locking and can be more predictable for simple rhythmic material.
tutor_behavior: A/B duplicate regions; do not make Smart the universal default.
what_decides: Arpeggios, pedal/CC data, flams, desired correction, and event complexity.

position_a: A straight grid gives clarity and predictable structure.
position_b: A groove template or retained microtiming may better match the musical pocket.
tutor_behavior: Choose the timing authority before moving notes.
what_decides: Genre, reference part, arrangement, and whether off-grid timing is intentional.

position_a: Quantize/Flex the performance to a fixed production grid.
position_b: Build a tempo map so programmed parts follow the expressive performance.
topic: Performance follows project versus project follows performance
tutor_behavior: Preserve the original and test both in a project alternative.
what_decides: Artistic rubato, later sequencing needs, genre, and editing complexity.

position_a: Full correction is appropriate for deliberately grid-locked material.
tutor_behavior: Start partial and increase until the problem stops distracting.
what_decides: Material role, performance quality, genre, and desired feel.

position_a: Region quantization is fast and consistent across repeated patterns.
position_b: Manual edits preserve intentional timing and target only real mistakes.
topic: Automatic quantization versus manual outlier edits
tutor_behavior: Use automatic correction only after a short representative test.
what_decides: Number of errors, consistency of pattern, ornaments, and artifact risk.

position_a: Small randomization can break sterile repetition.
position_b: Randomness can create sloppiness without musical phrasing.
tutor_behavior: Prefer retained performance or groove template; use bounded randomization sparingly.
what_decides: Pattern, role, amount, velocity/timing constraints, and reference groove.

position_a: Automatic region quantization is efficient for stable transient material.
position_b: Manual section edits reduce artifacts and preserve already-good timing.
topic: Whole-region audio quantization versus manual Flex edits
tutor_behavior: Test a short duplicate before processing the entire track.
what_decides: Source complexity, Flex algorithm, amount of correction, and artifact tolerance.
